role: In-memory stable-row-ID to physical RowAddress lookup, selecting a merged range map or a fragment-probing interval tree, with deletion filtering, per-segment accelerators, retained-memory accounting and unit/property fixtures. Public types are reexported from the otherwise private rowids::index module.
ranges: SPDX/imports connect Arc, inclusive ranges, Bitmap/count_ones, RowIdSequence/U64Segment, DeepSizeOf, RowAddress, DeletionVector, core errors and RangeInclusiveMap. Private MAX_PROBE_DEPTH=64 bounds overlapping fragment envelopes for the probe choice; MERGE_ROWS_BUDGET=1<<20 estimates rows read by merging; RANK_BLOCK_BYTES=256 means 2,048 bitmap slots per rank directory entry. Source comments' measured depth 46 is historical rationale, not a measurement from this task.

Public Debug RowIdIndex owns private sorted fragment entries, a max-end tree and optional merged RangeInclusiveMap<u64,(row-ID segment,address segment)>. Public FragmentRowIdIndex has public u32 fragment_id plus Arc<RowIdSequence> and Arc<DeletionVector>, without validation or a derive here. The opening comment says tombstoned addresses may be returned; current probe and merged construction actually filter supplied deletions, so the comment is stale. Empty deletion input naturally provides no such filtering.

Public new borrows a fragment-index slice, builds FragmentEntry/lookup sidecars for every nonempty source, sorts by lowest row ID and constructs the end tree before deciding representation. It builds a merged map unless probing_beats_merging returns true. Returns Result for duplicate-live-ID merge failures; input capacities, offsets and within-fragment uniqueness are not comprehensively validated. Both original fragment/sidecar state and the tree remain retained even when merged is Some.

build_merged clones Arc handles into temporary source descriptors, decomposes every source into chunks, eagerly collects them, groups overlapping numeric envelopes and merges only those groups. Nonoverlapping chunks pass through. Sparse bounds may overlap without live-ID collision, so duplicate detection examines enumerated IDs rather than span cardinality. Final chunks become RangeInclusiveMap. Construction materializes multiple intermediate vectors and may error after significant temporary allocation, but publishes no external state.

Public get(row_id:u64)->Result<Option<RowAddress>> dispatches to merged_get when a map exists, wrapping its Option in Ok, otherwise probes fragments. Thus merged cross-chunk duplicate errors happen at construction, while probe errors happen only for requested duplicated IDs. Missing IDs return None; no row bytes, file IO or mutable cache is accessed.

Public get_many allocates one None per input and returns it immediately for empty input. It builds/sorts a working Vec<(row_id,original_index)> and restores results to original positions, preserving input duplicates. Probe mode simply invokes self.probe for every sorted ID with no explicit persistent traversal cursor; first error aborts the whole call. The doc's O(F+N) amortization omits sorting and applies to merged chunk traversal, not total work in both modes.

Merged get_many walks sorted map chunks with a peekable iterator, advancing while range end < requested ID, skipping IDs before the next start and stopping when no chunks remain. Within a covering envelope it finds the row-ID segment position and corresponding address; either absence leaves None. Output remains in caller order. Work includes O(N log N) input sort plus chunk traversal and encoding-specific position/get costs; sparse envelope membership alone is not a live hit.

Private probe returns None for zero fragments or no start <= row ID. partition_point finds the candidate upper bound. An iterative stackless left-to-right DFS uses max-end tree values to prune subtrees, tests FragmentEntry::resolve at leaves, and continues after the first live hit to detect a second. Two hits return Internal naming the row ID. Ascending from right children adjusts lo/width; reaching root ends the walk, while lo>=upper terminates remaining sorted starts. No recursion or heap stack per lookup; worst work depends on overlapping envelopes and segment searches, not solely one binary search.

merged_get queries the range map, calls row-ID segment.position then address segment.get, converts raw address and returns None on either miss. Private SegmentEntry stores original sequence index, inclusive envelope, u32 starting physical offset and lookup. SegmentLookup::Native delegates to encoding; Positions stores sorted (ID,u32 position) pairs for unsorted arrays; BitmapRank stores u32 prefix popcounts per 256-byte block. These are memory-only accelerators, not serialized format fields.

SegmentEntry::position uses its original sequence index. Native delegates; Positions binary-searches ID and returns the saved offset. BitmapRank verifies the source variant and range, rejects a clear bit, then sums the directory prefix and bit count from the block start up to but excluding this bit. At most one 256-byte block prefix is scanned. It trusts valid bitmap storage, rank lengths and u32 offsets; malformed backing or stale sequence/sidecar correspondence can panic or misresolve. Arc ownership keeps ordinary safe mutation from changing this stored sequence.

build_lookup eagerly iterates Array into (ID,position as u32), sorts tuples and deduplicates by ID so the smallest original position wins; returned length remains the original segment length, not deduplicated count. Bitmap builds a rank directory and uses total counted ones as length; all other encodings use Native plus segment.len. Therefore construction does more than reading bounds: Array sidecars require full enumeration/sort and bitmap sidecars scan bytes even when probe mode is chosen.

build_bitmap_rank reserves ceil(data byte length/256) entries, stores cumulative ones cast to u32 before each chunk and counts all supplied bytes, returning directory and usize total. It does not mask logical trailing padding or validate bitmap.len; correctness relies on canonical bitmap storage. Private Debug FragmentEntry retains ID, Arc sequence/deletions, segment sidecars, min/max envelope and estimated merge_rows.

FragmentEntry::new iterates all sequence segments, builds lookup and len, counts len toward merge_rows whenever any deletion exists for the fragment or the segment is not a plain Range. Only positive-len segments with a reported range become entries; physical offset still advances for every segment. It computes min start/max end over retained segments or drops a source with none. u32 length casts and offset addition, u64 merge estimate addition are unchecked. Entirely deleted but physically nonempty sources may remain as probe candidates because deletion filtering occurs later.

FragmentEntry::resolve scans segments in sequence order, filters envelopes, asks the sidecar for a position, adds the segment start offset, then skips supplied deletion offsets. First surviving hit becomes RowAddress(fragment_id,physical_offset); later segments are not checked after that hit. Consequently this path detects cross-entry duplicates in probe, not every duplicate within one fragment; Positions collapses repeated IDs to their first original position. It preserves physical holes rather than compacting surviving offsets.

probing_beats_merging requires estimated merge rows strictly greater than 1,048,576 AND max envelope overlap depth <=64; exact budget or depth 65 selects merging. Short-circuit avoids overlap calculation below budget. max_overlap_depth sorts ends and sweeps start-sorted fragments, closing only end < next start because envelopes are inclusive. Depth counts fragment envelopes, including holes/deleted IDs, not exact live overlap. It assumes starts already sorted; totals use ordinary arithmetic.

build_end_tree returns empty Vec for no fragments; otherwise pads leaf count to next power of two, allocates 2*leaves zero u64s, stores fragment ends in leaves and fills internal maxima bottom-up. Index 0 is unused; root is 1. Padding zero may pass an ID-zero end check but is excluded by slot bounds. Capacity arithmetic/allocation are not fallible Result paths.

Manual DeepSizeOf traverses shared sequences/deletion vectors with the supplied Context, counts segment Vec capacity and Positions/BitmapRank allocation capacities, then estimates merged entries as two u64 bounds plus segment pair inline sizes and owned children. It adds fragment Vec/end-tree capacities. Arc dedup follows shared Context, but separately cached roots may each charge retained sequences. Range-map node/allocation overhead is not measured; this is an estimate, not exact RSS. Both probe accelerators and merged storage are charged when retained.

decompose_sequence starts at RowAddress::first_row(fragment_id), tracks u32 physical offset and u64 raw address, and chooses a no-deletion fast path only if the entire deletion vector is empty. After processing each segment, both offsets advance by its full physical length, including deleted rows; None chunks are filtered out. Length casts/additions are unchecked and no fragment-size bounds are validated here. Result is eagerly collected Vec.

build_chunk_from_pairs returns None for empty input, sorts (row ID,address) pairs by row ID, unzips into two owned Vecs, compresses each with U64Segment::from_iter and obtains inclusive coverage from the row-ID segment. Address order follows sorted IDs, preserving the original physical pairing. It does not explicitly reject duplicates within this single chunk; later overlapping-group merge is a separate check.

Without deletions a nonempty plain Range becomes cloned ID Range, arithmetic address Range and inclusive start..=end-1 in constant row-independent time. Empty segments return None. Every other encoding, including compact Ranges, is enumerated into pairs then sorted/compressed. Unchecked address end arithmetic assumes fragment lengths fit the RowAddress representation. Fast-path complexity is per segment, not total index construction including fragment/chunk sorting.

With deletions, every segment value is enumerated; local position plus current_offset is checked against DeletionVector, surviving values retain original raw address, then build_chunk_from_pairs sorts/compresses. Private IndexChunk aliases coverage plus ID/address segments. RawIndexChunk distinguishes one nonoverlapping chunk from an overlapping-envelope group; range_end extracts inclusive end. No tombstone is returned from either decomposition path when supplied deletion metadata is correct.

prep_index_chunks sorts all chunks by u64::MAX-start (descending start) and pops to process ascending starts. Empty input returns empty owned iterator; otherwise seed output with the first nonoverlapping chunk. It tracks a current overlapping group/envelope. Debug assertions repeatedly recompute minimum start/maximum end, using zero defaults for an empty group; these add debug-only work and encode internal grouping invariants.

When no group is active, compare next start <= previous output end. Overlap removes the previous nonoverlapping chunk, starts a two-chunk group and expands end; otherwise append it standalone. An active group absorbs any chunk starting within its current inclusive end, transitively extending the envelope; a gap flushes the group via replace/take then appends a standalone chunk. unwrap/unreachable rely on seeded-output/group state, not user validation.

Final debug assertions repeat group min/max agreement. Any remaining overlap group is appended, then the owned output Vec becomes an iterator. Adjacent but nonoverlapping inclusive envelopes are not grouped; sparse holes within overlapping bounds are handled later by live-ID merge. Despite its iterator return type, all grouping is completed and materialized before return.

merge_overlapping_chunks preallocates summed row-ID lengths, extends with zip of each ID/address iterator, stable-sorts by ID and rejects the first adjacent duplicate as Internal. Zip would truncate mismatched inputs; private decomposition is expected to maintain pairing. Duplicate check does not know actual fragment identities, so its multiple fragments message can also describe malformed overlapping chunks from one source. Rebuilds compressed ID/address segments and unwraps nonempty range, relying on nonempty overlap inputs.

cfg(test) RowIdIndex::probing bypasses the heuristic but still builds/sorts fragment sidecars and tree; its Result currently always succeeds. The tests module imports proptest. sparse_sequence makes even IDs in an explicit SortedArray; fragment wraps a sequence in Arc with empty deletion vector. Helpers are fixtures, not public construction alternatives.

Heuristic tests require a one-million-row plain Range and 16-element sparse sequence to merge, while a sparse sequence with budget+1 rows probes and resolves ID6 to offset3. A second fixture creates 65 interleaved fragments with just over the total row budget and requires merging despite build size. These tests establish selection thresholds in source, not measured performance or sub-second execution.

One test rejects duplicated live ID2 across two fragments during normal merged construction, then successfully probes only the first fragment; its name does not mean probe tolerates the same corrupt two-fragment input. The next forced-probe fixture uses both sources, resolves unique ID0, requires Internal plus the duplicate message for get(2), and requires get_many([0,2]) to error.

Bitmap rank test spans three full 2,048-slot blocks plus 17 slots, clears every slot congruent to1 mod3 and checks every live/missing lookup plus outside bounds. Unsorted-array probe fixture permutes 2,048 IDs by multiply7919 modulo2048 and asserts every original physical position, keeping merged None. Neither test benchmarks latency.

test_new_index combines fragment10 Range/holes/sorted-array segments with fragment20 bitmap/Array segments. Assertions check first values, omitted IDs15/61, end-of-hole rank and cumulative offsets across segments: ID25 at fragment10 offset16, ID40/60 at fragment20 offsets2/4. Both deletion vectors are empty; holes are sequence representation gaps.

test_new_index_overlap interleaves IDs1..9 across fragments10/42/23 with overlapping sparse envelopes, then asserts all nine exact fragment/offset pairs. This verifies valid overlapping envelopes merge without requiring dense ownership by one fragment.

Unsorted fixture supplies [9,3,6], [8,2,5] and [7,1,4] across fragments10/20/30 as explicit Arrays. It verifies all nine IDs map to original physical positions after sorting the merged ID dimension, and IDs0/10 are absent. This tests pairing preservation, not sorted-input assumptions.

Partial-overlap fixture has fragment0 RangeWithHoles(0..100, hole50) and fragment1 Range50..51. It checks ownership of50 by fragment1 and fragment0 offsets before/after the hole (ID51 at50, ID99 at98). Sequence holes do not occupy physical positions, unlike deletion-vector holes.

Sparse-overlap deletion fixture alternates odd/even IDs across two fragments and tombstones even-source offset2 (ID4). It asserts ID4 missing and surviving IDs6/8 retain physical offsets3/4. Thus overlapping span union may have holes and deletion filtering must not renumber surviving addresses.

Single Range0..6 with deletion offsets2/3 returns addresses for0/1/4/5 at unchanged offsets and None for2/3. This directly contradicts the stale type comment that this index can return supplied tombstoned addresses.

Empty-fragment fixture mixes no segments with Range5..8 and checks live boundary lookup plus missing4. Completely empty constructor returns an index whose get(0) and get(100) are None. No error is expected from empty inputs.

Three adjacent nonoverlapping ranges0..5,5..10,10..15 across fragments10/20/30 assert each first/last physical offset. Inclusive coverage boundaries derived from exclusive ranges must not cause false overlap or off-by-one mapping.

arbitrary_row_ids generates fragment sizes in supplied ranges, constructs globally unique IDs0..sum, shuffles all IDs, partitions by sizes and compresses each sequence. Fragment IDs are cumulative starting row positions cast to u32, not sequential fragment ordinal; zero-size sources may reuse a cumulative ID but hold no rows. Strategy materializes the global ID Vec.

arbitrary_row_ids_with_deletions pairs the generated sources with one arbitrary bool per physical row, then consumes those flags in source/offset order into Roaring deletion bitmaps. Each result retains its Arc sequence and a Bitmap deletion vector, possibly empty. Test generation uses unwrap under guaranteed vector cardinality and bounded inputs.

Large-range regression constructs100 fragments of250,000 rows (25 million total) without deletions, times only RowIdIndex::new and asserts selected boundaries plus missing final+1. It requires elapsed.as_secs()<1. The comment's typically<1ms and O(fragments) language are rationale, not observed here; range decomposition is row-independent but fragment/chunk sorting still exists. This test was not run.

Large-deletion fixture uses10 fragments of1,000 rows with every third physical offset removed, checks missing0/3/next-fragment-start/last-row and unchanged survivor offsets including final998. It checks final out-of-range too. No timing assertion in this test; it exercises deletion-aware enumeration and mapping.

Proptest robustness generates0..4 fragments each0..31 rows with deletions, constructs both heuristic and forced-probe indices, and checks every generated physical ID against an explicit deletion/address oracle. It covers both representations on small fixtures, not malformed global duplicates or all sidecar encodings by guarantee.

Moved-ID property chooses any u64 row ID, source fragment below1024 and positive delta below1024, marks source offset0 deleted and target live. New merged index must resolve to target offset0. This includes u64::MAX candidates through the generator and establishes live uniqueness rather than physical-history uniqueness.

Duplicate-live property creates two distinct fragments holding the same arbitrary u64 ID without deletions. Construction must fail with Internal and exact ID context. It tests merged validation on small sources; forced probe's delayed duplicate behavior is tested separately.

Range-segment fixture excludes1200..1900 from1000..3000, asserts use_range_segments changes representation, then verifies every remaining ID's ordinal address and missing1500. get_many on [2999,1000,1199,1900,1500] must preserve requested order and return last,0,199,200,None. This is the file's explicit successful batch-lookup case; there is no broad get_many property matrix, retained-size fixture or overflow/padding-corruption test here.
limits: All 1,641 physical lines were read and authored. This synchronous structure uses no unsafe blocks, locks, awaits or object IO. Segment/bitmap/deletion/RowAddress contracts are separately documented; no source tests or benchmarks were executed. Heuristic thresholds and test timing assertions are source facts, not verified latency promises. Complete Dataset construction/caching/refresh and scan callers remain pending; the benchmark is analyzed separately.
